t2i_prompt: A wide web page section on a deep navy background framed as an engineering drawing sheet with a thin border, zone ticks and title-block tables in the corners. On the left, a very large light-weight sans-serif headline in off-white. On the right, a vertical stack of square-cornered outlined boxes, one per item: <CONTENT>. Behind everything, faint low-opacity P&ID fragments, small isometric vessels and ruled tables in pale blue hairlines. One translucent steel-blue pipe ribbon is the only bright accent. A short monospace list of reference codes sits bottom right. Flat vector, straight-on, no people.
signature_idea: A big calm headline sitting on a ghosted drawing sheet, with the choices stacked as framed boxes and the standards codes set in mono like a title block.
strengths: strong hierarchy: headline first, three choices second
monospace standard codes speak directly to validation leads
background schematics add domain authenticity without competing (mostly)
outlined boxes are simple to build as a router or tab set
weaknesses: background collage is noisy and random; schematics do not relate to the three industries
evidence text per industry is missing, so the core point is not made
the pipe ribbon looks pasted on and stylistically inconsistent
boxes have uneven internal rules and look like broken tables
brand_fit_why: Light big headline, mono codes, navy and square corners are on-brand, but the cluttered ghost-schematic collage works against 'calm' and 'space as a material'.
